concepts.heading: What Is Intersectionality?
concepts.alt: Four guides standing where several coloured roads cross, looking at the crossing together
concepts.plain: Intersectionality means the parts of who you are overlap and shape your life together.

concepts.heading: Intersectionality Applied to Intimacy
concepts.alt: A guide holding overlapping coloured see-through circles that form a heart in the middle
concepts.plain: Those overlaps also shape desire, safety and who gets good care.

concepts.heading: Why One-Size-Fits-All Approaches Fail
concepts.alt: A guide holding up a tiny t-shirt that clearly does not fit him, shrugging with a smile
concepts.plain: Most sex ed was written for one kind of person, so it leaves many people out.

concepts.heading: Intersectionality Is Not Ranking Oppressions
concepts.plain: This is not a contest over who has it worst. It is a way to understand each person.

options: A ranking of who has it worst
How overlapping parts of who you are shape your experience
checks.explanation: How overlapping parts of who you are shape your experience. In 1989, legal scholar Kimberlé Crenshaw coined the term "intersectionality" to describe how Black women experience overlapping systems of oppression that cannot be understood by examining race and gender separately.

checks.prompt: Who was most mainstream sexuality education designed for?
checks.explanation: One narrow kind of person. Most mainstream sexuality education was designed with a specific audience in mind.

166040f6-ffb0-4de4-9658-548fc51c49e3.takeaway: Parts of who you are, like race, gender and disability, combine to shape your love life.

concepts.heading: How Race Shapes Intimate Experience
concepts.alt: Two guides talking warmly over cups of tea
concepts.plain: Race and culture affect how people experience attraction and relationships.

concepts.heading: Racial Fetishization
concepts.alt: A guide holding up a hand in a calm stop gesture beside a crossed-out blank sticky label
concepts.plain: Fetishizing means wanting someone for a racial stereotype instead of who they are.

concepts.heading: Racial Preferences in Dating
concepts.alt: A guide looking thoughtfully into a hand mirror
concepts.plain: "Just a preference" is worth a closer look. Tastes are shaped by what we were shown.

concepts.heading: Interracial Intimacy
concepts.alt: Two guides holding hands and smiling at each other
concepts.plain: Couples from different backgrounds share real joys and face real challenges.

concepts.heading: The Impact of Colonialism
concepts.plain: A lot of sexual shame around the world was spread by colonial rule.

concepts.heading: Race in ENM Spaces
concepts.alt: Four guides sitting in a circle of chairs, warmly offering one empty chair to a newcomer
concepts.plain: Our own communities need to look honestly at who feels welcome and who does not.

checks.prompt: Racial fetishization means attraction based mainly on…
options: Racial stereotypes rather than the actual person
checks.explanation: Racial stereotypes rather than the actual person. Racial fetishization occurs when attraction to someone is primarily based on racial stereotypes rather than on the actual person.

checks.prompt: Where do many global attitudes of sexual shame have roots?
checks.explanation: In colonialism. Many global attitudes about sexuality — shame around pleasure, rigid gender roles, persecution of LGBTQ+ people — have roots in colonialism.

a6724f88-73ad-461c-b7cb-8c2a8f57c878.takeaway: Race and culture shape dating and desire. Treat people as people, not as types.

concepts.heading: Disability and Sexuality: An AASECT Core Competency
concepts.plain: Sex educators are expected to understand disability. It is a core skill.

concepts.heading: Challenging Desexualization
concepts.alt: A guide sitting in a wheelchair dressed up for a date, holding a rose and smiling confidently
concepts.plain: Disabled people are often treated as if they have no sexual side. That is false.

concepts.heading: Physical Disability and Sexuality
concepts.alt: A in a wheelchair and B sitting beside her, holding hands and laughing
concepts.plain: A physical disability can change how sex works. Different does not mean less.

concepts.heading: Neurodiversity and Intimacy
concepts.alt: A guide wearing headphones, calm and happy, with soft sparkles around his head
concepts.plain: Brains that work differently experience touch, talk and closeness differently.

concepts.heading: Nothing About Us Without Us
concepts.alt: Around a table planning together, A in a wheelchair leading the discussion
concepts.plain: Disabled people should lead the decisions that affect them.

checks.prompt: What is the "desexualization" of disabled people?
options: Assuming they have no sexual desires or needs
checks.explanation: Assuming they have no sexual desires or needs. One of the most pervasive forms of ableism in sexuality is the desexualization of disabled people — the assumption that people with disabilities are not sexual beings, do not experience desire, and should not be considered as romantic or…

options: Disabled people should shape what is made for them
checks.explanation: Disabled people should shape what is made for them. The disability rights principle "nothing about us without us" applies directly to sexuality education and community building.

d36b08a4-5fe0-4a78-8ea6-33e5c5b31277.takeaway: Disabled and neurodivergent people have full sexual lives and should help shape the spaces meant for them.

concepts.heading: From Diversity to Genuine Inclusion
concepts.alt: A guide opening a door wide and waving others in
concepts.plain: Saying "everyone is welcome" is easy. Making it true takes work.

concepts.heading: How ENM and Kink Spaces Reproduce Exclusion
concepts.alt: A guide looking up at a tall stack of gold coins blocking a doorway
concepts.plain: Even open-minded spaces shut people out, through cost, access and who is in charge.

concepts.heading: Practical Steps for Creating Inclusive Spaces
concepts.alt: Four guides building a wooden ramp together up to a doorway
concepts.plain: Organizers can lower costs, make venues accessible and share leadership.

concepts.heading: When Intersectional Concerns Arise in Relationships
concepts.alt: Two guides sitting facing each other, listening closely, one hand on heart
concepts.plain: In a relationship, different life experiences can cause friction. Listen and believe.

concepts.heading: Professional Support
concepts.plain: Look for helpers who understand race, disability, gender and more together.

checks.after: How ENM and Kink Spaces Reproduce Exclusion
checks.prompt: Name one way ENM and kink spaces can shut people out.
checks.explanation: Cost barriers. Events and classes cost money, which keeps some people out even in spaces that value openness.

checks.after: When Intersectional Concerns Arise in Relationships
checks.prompt: Can differences in identity create tension inside a relationship?
options: Yes, and it helps to name them
checks.explanation: Yes, and it helps to name them. Partners can experience the world very differently, and that can create tension between them.

2d2958c6-cb8a-4c78-8242-5732dd96c5fe.takeaway: Welcoming everyone takes action: lower the barriers and share the lead.
